questions.stem: In this task, you are to write an essay on the importance o f developing a healthy lifestyle among college students. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
A healthy lifestyle plays a vital role in the life of every college student. As campus life grows busier with assignments and screens, I firmly believe that keeping fit, eating well and sleeping regularly is not a trivial habit but the very foundation of a successful university experience.

For one thing, a sound body directly boosts learning efficiency. A student who stays up all night rushing a due date and lives on takeout will struggle to concentrate the next morning, while regular exercise and balanced meals keep the mind sharp in class. For another, a healthy routine stabilizes our emotions. Sitting still for hours breeds anxiety, whereas a short run often washes away the pressure of exams and eases loneliness far from home.

In conclusion, a healthy lifestyle is not optional but essential for college students. The sooner we build it, the more energy and confidence we will carry into our studies and future lives.

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: The World Pipe Band Championships will take place in Glasgow on Saturday.
transcript.zh: 世界风笛乐队锦标赛将于周六在格拉斯哥举行。

transcript.text: Over 120 of the world's best pipe bands will compete at the championships. Over 4,000 pipers and drummers are expected to descend on the city for the annual event.
transcript.zh: 超过120支世界顶尖风笛乐队将参加锦标赛。预计超过4000名风笛手和鼓手将涌入该市参加这一年度盛事。

transcript.text: It will take place at the St. James Playing Fields in Glasgow on Saturday, 18 May from 10:00 am until 7:00 pm. The event is free. Also, a free shuttle bus will run between the event car parks and the competition site. Shuttle buses will run every 15 minutes from 8:00 am until 8:00 pm.
transcript.zh: 比赛将于5月18日周六上午10点至晚上7点在格拉斯哥的St. James运动场举行。该活动免费入场。此外,将有免费班车往返于活动停车场和比赛场地之间。班车从上午8点至晚上8点每15分钟一班。

transcript.text: Glasgow City Council says it is estimated to bring £300,000 to the local economy.
transcript.zh: 格拉斯哥市议会表示,预计该活动将为当地经济带来30万英镑的收益。

transcript.text: The first World Pipe Band Championships were held in Edinburgh in 1947. The event first took place in Glasgow in 1948. It has been held regularly in Glasgow since 1986.
transcript.zh: 首届世界风笛乐队锦标赛于1947年在爱丁堡举行。该活动于1948年首次在格拉斯哥举办。自1986年以来一直定期在格拉斯哥举行。

questions.stem: What event will take place in Glasgow?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The World Pipe Band Championships will take place in Glasgow on Saturday.信号：开篇点题句 。新闻首句 The World Pipe Band Championships will take place in Glasgow on Saturday. 与题干 What event will ta…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音通篇没出现任何 car show、汽车相关表述，A free car show. 属凭空想象。它唯一沾边的是 free 这个词——录音里 The event is free. 确实说了 free，于是把「免费」错按到「车展」上，是典型的把原词嫁接到错对象。 借用原文：the annual event
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：录音说的是 the annual event，annual 与选项里的 yearly 同义，但核心活动是 pipe band championships，不是 concert(音乐会)。yearly 这个原义被偷出来盖到一个录音从未提到的 concert 上。 借用原文：Over 120 of the world's best pipe bands will compete at the championships.
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：A sports competition. 中 competition 与 D 项的 contest 几乎同义——录音里的 Championships 翻译成 competition 也讲得通，但风笛比赛属于音乐文化赛事，不是体育(sports)赛事。把 sports 这一定语换成 pipe band 才对。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（The World Pipe Band Championships ↔ A pipe band contest championships 同义替换为 contest）

questions.evidenceText: The World Pipe Band Championships will take place in Glasgow on Saturday.

questions.stem: What does Glasgow City Council say the event will do?

options.text: Improve the image of Glasgow city.
Enrich the local culture of Glasgow.
Contribute a lot to the local economy.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：Glasgow City Council says it is estimated to bring £300,000 to the local economy.信号：题干主语 + 金额词同时命中 。原文 Glasgow City Council says it is estimated to bring £300,000 to the local economy. 与题干 Wha…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：录音通篇无 image / reputation 等谈论城市形象的字眼。它和 C 在「为城市好」的方向上同方向，容易让考生「感觉对」，但题目问的是 Council 实际说了什么，没说就是没说。
optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：录音里 The first World Pipe Band Championships were held in Edinburgh in 1947. 等句确实交代了赛事历史，乍听有文化色彩，但「丰富格拉斯哥本地文化」 (Enrich the local culture of Glasgow.) 这一定性并不是 Glasgow City Council 给的，更不是题干所问。 借用原文：Over 4,000 pipers and drummers are expected to descend on the city for the annual event.
optionAnalysis.D: 过度推断：录音里 Over 4,000 pipers and drummers are expected to descend on the city for the annual event. 说的是有 4000 名风笛手鼓手前来参赛，并未提及「娱乐当地社区居民」。选项把「热闹场面」这一表象误读成「让 local communities 开心」，方向偏。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（bring £300,000 to the local economy ↔ Contribute a lot to the local economy. bring 金额 = contribute a lot）

questions.evidenceText: Glasgow City Council says it is estimated to bring £300,000 to the local economy.

transcript.text: Summer doesn't begin for two more days, but scientists are already sounding the alarm about dangerous ice melts going on right now in Greenland.
transcript.zh: 距离夏季开始还有两天,但科学家们已经对格陵兰岛目前正在发生的危险冰层融化发出警报。

transcript.text: The vast island usually locks away enough fresh water in its ice sheet, which if melted can raise global sea levels by six meters. And research shows that in recent years its ice has melted faster than ever before. This month, as temperatures in northwestern Greenland approach all-time highs, researchers are encountering unusual, surprising levels of melting ice in the region.
transcript.zh: 这座广袤的岛屿通常将足够多的淡水锁在其冰盖中,如果融化可使全球海平面上升六米。研究表明,近年来其冰层融化速度比以往任何时候都快。本月,随着格陵兰岛西北部气温接近历史最高值,研究人员在该地区遇到了异常且令人惊讶的冰层融化水平。

transcript.text: The most significant concern here is how early this is all happening. Greenland experiences annual ice melt and growth cycles. But this year, the melting season began in early May. That's a month earlier than normal and something that's happened only once before in the historical record in 2016.
transcript.zh: 这里最重大的担忧是这一切发生得如此之早。格陵兰岛经历着年度冰层融化和增长周期。但今年,融化季节始于五月初。这比正常情况提前了一个月,而且在历史记录中只在2016年发生过一次。

transcript.text: That means that not only is the ice melting very fast, it has more time to melt this summer than it would in a normal climate system. Longer melt seasons like this one seem to lead to much greater contributions to sea-level rise than in previous decades.
transcript.zh: 这意味着冰层不仅融化得非常快,而且今年夏天它有比正常气候系统中更多的时间融化。像这样更长的融化季节似乎会导致对海平面上升的贡献远大于前几十年。

questions.stem: What is scientists' warning in the news report?

options.text: Surprising rise in global sea levels.
Record growth of Greenland's ice sheets.

questions.analysis: 主旨题。答案句（P1）：Summer doesn't begin for two more days, but scientists are already sounding the alarm about dangerous ice melts going on right now in Greenland.信号：导语 + 转折 but + sounding the alarm 。答案信号有三层叠加：第一，这是新闻第一句（导语，新闻惯例第一句点题）；第二，句中 but 是强转折，新闻里 but 之后才是真正要说的事；第三，紧跟…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 借用原文第 2 段 raise global sea levels by six meters 里的 sea levels 做诱饵，但原文那句只是『如果冰盖融化，可能抬升海平面 6 米』，是一个假设性的后果，且 surprising rise in global sea levels 并未在录音中实际宣布，把『潜在后果』当成『已经发生的警告』，属偷换概念。 借用原文：Summer doesn't begin for two more days
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：C 盗用原文里 Summer 与第 3、4 段反复出现的『季节、夏季』语境，把话题悄悄从『冰融』扩大到『夏季天气模式的变化』。整则新闻没有讨论 weather patterns（如降雨、风暴等气象格局），范围被无故放大。 借用原文：its ice has melted faster than ever before
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：D 把录音里 ice melts、ice sheet 这些原词搬过来，但把动作整个反过来说成 record growth of Greenland's ice sheets（『创纪录地增长』），与原文 its ice has melted faster than ever before 方向相反，是典型的『反向』诱饵。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（sounding the alarm ↔ scientists' warning 拉响警报等于发出警告）

questions.evidenceText: Summer doesn't begin for two more days, but scientists are already sounding the alarm about dangerous ice melts going on right now in Greenland.

questions.stem: What do we learn about this year's ice melting?

options.text: It started a month earlier than usual.
It ended a month earlier than before.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：But this year, the melting season began in early May. That's a month earlier than normal and something that's happened only once before in the historical record in 2016.信号：转折 But this year 加时间反常 。信号有两层：第一，But this year 是强转折，前面在讲『通常的融冰周期』，But 一拐就来到『今年反常』的落点；第二，紧跟出现的 a month earlie…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 借用原文 began in early May 里的 May 做诱饵，但把 early May（5 月初）偷换成 late May（5 月底）；只要听清 early 与 late 这一字之差，就能识破。 借用原文：the melting season began in early May
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 项 It lasted three months. 在录音中完全没有出现『三个月』或任何与 three months 对应的时长表述，是利用考生听到 Longer melt seasons 就想去补一个具体时长的心理凭空捏造的数字。
optionAnalysis.D: 与原文相反：D 与正确项 C 只差一个动词：started 变 ended。原文清清楚楚说的是融冰季『开始』提前一个月（began in early May），而非『结束』提前一个月；D 把动作整个反向，是典型的『开始或结束』互换陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the melting season began in early May ↔ It started a month earlier than usual. began 对应 started）

questions.evidenceText: But this year, the melting season began in early May. That's a month earlier than normal and something that's happened only once before in the historical record in 2016.

transcript.text: Bundles containing thousands of pounds in cash keep turning up on the streets of Blackhall Colliery in northern England, according to police. Residents of the village have been coming across bundles of £20 notes—usually worth £2,000—in the former mining village in County Durham.
transcript.zh: 据警方称,在英格兰北部的Blackhall Colliery街道上不断出现装有数千英镑现金的捆包。这个村庄的居民一直在Durham郡这个前矿业村发现成捆的20英镑纸币——通常价值2000英镑。

transcript.text: The latest discovery was on Monday, meaning four of these cash bundles have been handed in this year and 13 since 2014.
transcript.zh: 最近一次发现是在周一,这意味着今年已有四个这样的现金捆包被上交,自2014年以来共有13个。

transcript.text: The bundles are usually left in plain sight and have been scattered across the small coastal village. The owner has two weeks to collect the cash, which is then returned to the finder if not claimed, according to Peterlee Police.
transcript.zh: 这些捆包通常被放置在显眼位置,散布在这个沿海小村庄各处。据Peterlee警方称,失主有两周时间来认领现金,如果无人认领,现金将归还给发现者。

transcript.text: A Durham Police spokesperson said the money has been returned to the lucky finders in all cases except yesterday.
transcript.zh: Durham警方发言人表示,除了昨天的情况外,所有案例中的钱款都已归还给幸运的发现者。

transcript.text: Policeman John Forster said in a statement: "The circumstances remain a mystery so we would welcome any information that will help us get to the bottom of these random incidents."
transcript.zh: 警察John Forster在一份声明中说:"具体情况仍是一个谜,因此我们欢迎任何能帮助我们查明这些随机事件真相的信息。"

transcript.text: He told The Northern Echo: "It isn't an affluent part of the world, so for them to find cash of that amount and instantly think about taking it to the police stations shows the community spirit there is."
transcript.zh: 他告诉The Northern Echo:"这里并不是一个富裕的地方,所以他们发现那么多现金后立即想到送到警察局,这显示了当地的社区精神。"

questions.stem: What happened on the streets of Blackhall Colliery?

options.text: Bundles of £20 notes kept turning up.
A villager was searching for his lost cash.
Local policemen came across bundles of £20 notes.
A bundle containing thousands of pounds got stolen.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Bundles containing thousands of pounds in cash keep turning up on the streets of Blackhall Colliery in northern England, according to police.信号：新闻导语首句即落点 。答案信号是"导语首句"：Bundles containing thousands of pounds in cash keep turning up on the streets 正是全篇第一句…

optionAnalysis.B: B 说 A villager was searching for his lost cash.（一名村民在找他丢失的现金），但录音是钱不断"出现"、村民是"捡到"，从无谁在"找丢失的钱"，方向与原文相反。
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 盗用了录音原词 came across 与 policemen 拼成 Local policemen came across bundles of £20 notes.，但原文是 Residents of the village have been coming across bundles of £20 notes——"撞见"现金的是村民居民，不是警察，把发现者张冠李戴了。 借用原文：Bundles containing thousands of pounds in cash
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 说 A bundle containing thousands of pounds got stolen.（一捆数千英镑被偷），盗用了原文 Bundles containing thousands of pounds 的措辞，却把"出现并被上交"歪曲成"被偷"，与全篇"现金被发现、还给失主"的事实相反。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（keep turning up on the streets ↔ kept turning up 时态变体的同一短语）

questions.evidenceText: Bundles containing thousands of pounds in cash keep turning up on the streets of Blackhall Colliery in northern England, according to police.

questions.stem: What do the local police do with the money if not claimed in two weeks?

options.text: They return it to the finder.
They hand it over to the local government.
They place a notice in The Northern Echo.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The owner has two weeks to collect the cash, which is then returned to the finder if not claimed, according to Peterlee Police.信号：条件状语后的处置动词 。答案信号是条件 + 处置动词：which is then returned to the finder if not claimed 里 if not claimed（若无人认领）正对题干 n…

optionAnalysis.A: A 说 They give it to charity.（捐给慈善），录音通篇没出现 charity 或捐赠的说法，是凭"无主之财常做公益"的常识硬填，属未提及。
optionAnalysis.C: C 说 hand it over to the local government（上交当地政府），录音里出现的是 Peterlee Police、Durham Police 这些警方，从未说交给 local government（地方政府），把接收对象张冠李戴了。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：D 说 place a notice in The Northern Echo（在《北方回声报》登启事），盗用了录音原词 The Northern Echo，但那是警察 John Forster 后文受访的报纸，与"无人认领后怎么处置钱"毫无关系，答非所问。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（returned to the finder ↔ return it to the finder 被动转主动的同一动作）

questions.evidenceText: The owner has two weeks to collect the cash, which is then returned to the finder if not claimed, according to Peterlee Police.

questions.stem: What did the policeman John Forster say about the villagers?

options.text: They cooperated well with the police.
They enjoyed a fairly affluent life.
They were puzzled by the mystery.
They had a strong community spirit.

questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P6）：It isn't an affluent part of the world, so for them to find cash of that amount and instantly think about taking it to the police stations shows the community spirit there is.信号：so…shows 引出结论评价 。答案信号是"因果连词 so + 总结动词 shows"：so for them to find cash…instantly think about taking it to the…

optionAnalysis.A: A 说 They cooperated well with the police.（他们与警方配合良好），录音里村民确有"把钱送去警局"的行为，但 Forster 并未据此评价他们"配合警方"，而是上升为社区精神——A 是对行为的过度推断。
optionAnalysis.B: B 说 They enjoyed a fairly affluent life.（过着相当富裕的生活），盗用了录音原词 affluent，但原文是 It isn't an affluent part of the world——明明说"不富裕"，B 把否定去掉、反了极性。 借用原文：The circumstances remain a mystery
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 说 They were puzzled by the mystery.（他们被这谜团困惑），盗用了录音原词 The circumstances remain a mystery 的 mystery，但感到费解的是警方（Forster 说 remain a mystery、想 get to the bottom），不是村民，把困惑者张冠李戴了。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（shows the community spirit there is ↔ They had a strong community spirit. 结论原词直接对应）

questions.evidenceText: It isn't an affluent part of the world, so for them to find cash of that amount and instantly think about taking it to the police stations shows the community spirit there is.

transcript.text: W: It's your birthday next week. What have you got planned?
transcript.zh: W: 下周就是你的生日了。你有什么计划吗？

transcript.text: M: I'm not sure. I often feel strange on my birthday. It's like my brain decides to have a crisis.
transcript.zh: M: 我还不确定。我在生日的时候经常感觉怪怪的。就好像我的大脑决定要来一场危机。

transcript.text: W: It's not entirely unusual to feel anxious or sad around your birthday. Birthdays can tap into a lot of things people worry about, including their achievements in life in the past decade, or their accomplishments of the past year. Many begin to search for the meaning of their existence, leading to behaviors such as ending or starting a relationship, or plans, like starting a vigorous diet or fitness program.
transcript.zh: W: 在生日前后感到焦虑或悲伤并不完全罕见。生日会触及人们担心的很多事情，包括他们过去十年的人生成就，或者过去一年的成绩。许多人开始寻找自己存在的意义，导致一些行为，比如结束或开始一段关系，或者制定计划，比如开始严格的饮食或健身计划。

transcript.text: M: I have wonderful friends and I love celebrating their birthdays. But I don't like being the center of attention, receiving gifts and having a fuss made. It seems to trigger a type of social anxiety. I think social media too can intensify things as birthdays now play out more publicly. Birthday reminders can be helpful, but I kind of worry I won't be able to drum up my own day and show it to look as exciting as it is supposed to be.
transcript.zh: M: 我有很棒的朋友，我也喜欢庆祝他们的生日。但我不喜欢成为关注的焦点，收礼物，被大家围着忙活。这似乎会引发一种社交焦虑。我觉得社交媒体也会让事情更严重，因为现在生日更多是公开展示的。生日提醒可能有帮助,但我有点担心我没法把自己的生日搞得看起来像应该的那么激动人心。

transcript.text: W: Well, to deal with the birthday blues, you should not isolate yourself. It's best to gradually face your birthday with people you trust. That would help you learn self-acceptance, or that it's okay to be the focus.
transcript.zh: W: 嗯，要应对生日忧郁，你不应该把自己孤立起来。最好是和你信任的人一起逐渐面对你的生日。这会帮助你学会自我接纳，或者说成为焦点也没关系。

transcript.text: M: Perhaps. Or I could perceive my birthday as an opportunity to do something for others like asking people to make a donation instead of buying a gift.
transcript.zh: M: 也许吧。或者我可以把生日看作是为别人做点什么的机会，比如请人们捐款而不是买礼物。

transcript.text: W: Exactly. Or even simply see your birthday as an opportunity to bring people together for them to have fun.
transcript.zh: W: 没错。或者甚至可以简单地把你的生日看作是把大家聚在一起让他们开心的机会。

questions.stem: How does the man often feel on his birthday?
questions.analysis: 态度观点题。答案句（P2）：I often feel strange on my birthday. It's like my brain decides to have a crisis.信号：被问者的直接应答 + 原话情绪词 。女士先问"生日有什么打算"，男士开口就答 I often feel strange on my birthday，这是被问者的直接应答，且 often feel strange 几…

optionAnalysis.A: 未提及：Excited. 是大家默认"过生日该有"的情绪，靠常识容易误选，但录音男士从头到尾没说兴奋，反而说怪怪的、像要闹危机，与 A 相反。
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：Delighted.(高兴)同样是想当然的"生日心情"，录音并未表达欢喜，男士说的是 strange，故排除。
optionAnalysis.C: 偷换概念：Indifferent.(无所谓)看似贴近"不太在乎生日"，但录音说的是 feel strange、brain has a crisis，是"心绪不宁"而非"无所谓"，态度强度对不上。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（I often feel strange on my birthday ↔ Strange. 原词直接对应）

questions.evidenceText: I often feel strange on my birthday. It's like my brain decides to have a crisis.

questions.stem: What does the woman say many people tend to do on their birthday?

options.text: Search for the meaning of their life.
Look back on their years at school.
Call on their relatives and friends.

transcript.text: Steve Miller began his career in IT back in the late 1980s. Being a deaf person in tech required a huge amount of effort in organization. Because there was no email or text message service, everything had to be done face to face, or by telephone. Communicating in meetings was very difficult. He needed a sign language interpreter for every meeting, but it was a huge effort to coordinate.
transcript.zh: Steve Miller 在 20 世纪 80 年代末开始了他的 IT 职业生涯。作为一名科技行业的失聪人士,需要在组织协调方面付出巨大努力。因为那时没有电子邮件或短信服务,一切都必须面对面进行,或者通过电话完成。在会议中交流非常困难。他每次会议都需要一名手语翻译,但协调这件事需要付出巨大努力。

transcript.text: These days, although challenges still remain, it's a good time to be a deaf person in tech, says Miller. Big advances in speech recognition technology have enabled communication tools to turn live speech into text in real time on your smartphone or laptop, and sign language into text as well.
transcript.zh: Miller 说,如今尽管挑战依然存在,但对于科技行业的失聪人士来说是个好时代。语音识别技术的重大进步使得通信工具能够在智能手机或笔记本电脑上实时将现场语音转换为文本,也能将手语转换为文本。

transcript.text: New Tech coupled with improvements in hearing aid technology and medical advances means that Miller is able to focus far more on his work. He has benefited to a great extent from a tiny hearing device in his ear. It gives him a degree of hearing, and he can use a variety of communication methods depending on the situation. He can employ lip-reading and have meetings via video instead of on the phone. These things have made a huge difference. He no longer has to worry about whether or not he can understand. He can just concentrate on how interesting the meeting might be and what he needs to get out of it in order to progress.
transcript.zh: 新技术加上助听器技术的改进和医学进步,意味着 Miller 能够更加专注于他的工作。他从耳中的一个微型助听设备中获益匪浅。它给了他一定程度的听力,他可以根据情况使用各种交流方式。他可以使用唇读,通过视频而不是电话进行会议。这些事情带来了巨大的改变。他不再需要担心自己能否理解。他可以只专注于会议可能有多有趣,以及他需要从中获得什么才能取得进展。

transcript.text: Colour is now spreading through our homes, up staircases, across wood frames and ceilings, filling in neutral spaces.
transcript.zh: 色彩正在我们的家中蔓延，爬上楼梯，延伸至木框架和天花板，填充着中性色空间。

transcript.text: According to one interior designer, when people return home, they want to see colours that cheer them up and give them a hug. Pure white walls simply don't do that. They don't look after you.
transcript.zh: 据一位室内设计师说,当人们回到家时,他们想看到能让他们振奋精神、给予他们拥抱的色彩。纯白色的墙壁根本做不到这一点。它们不会照顾你。

transcript.text: Another interior designer commented that certain combinations can key into something on a deeper level, transporting you to a different moment in time. That's the power of colour.
transcript.zh: 另一位室内设计师评论说,某些色彩组合可以触及更深层次的东西,将你带到不同的时刻。这就是色彩的力量。

transcript.text: If you are thinking to try colour on some of your neutral walls, the advice is refreshingly simple: Choose a colour you actually like.
transcript.zh: 如果你正在考虑在一些中性色墙面上尝试色彩,建议非常简单:选择一个你真正喜欢的颜色。

transcript.text: Don't go for a colour because it's in fashion, or you've seen it in a magazine.
transcript.zh: 不要因为某种颜色流行或你在杂志上看到过就选择它。

transcript.text: If you're weary of full colour, test your tolerance with smaller spaces, such as the inside of a cupboard or a bright window frame. If it gives you joy every time you open the cupboard, you can start to take it further.
transcript.zh: 如果你对全彩色心存疑虑,可以用较小的空间测试你的接受度,比如橱柜内部或明亮的窗框。如果每次打开橱柜它都能给你带来快乐,你就可以开始进一步尝试。

transcript.text: One can also paint the wooden frameworks the same colour as the walls, helping the rooms look bigger. In the kitchen, painting the overhead cupboards and the walls in the same colour can make it feel more spacious.
transcript.zh: 人们还可以将木框架漆成与墙壁相同的颜色,帮助房间看起来更大。在厨房里,将吊柜和墙壁漆成相同的颜色可以让空间感觉更宽敞。

transcript.text: While painting the kitchen counters, a bold colour can make everything feel more open and lighter. Additionally, a painted ceiling is a magical thing without being too obvious and can affect how the space feels as well.
transcript.zh: 在粉刷厨房台面时,大胆的色彩可以让一切感觉更开阔、更轻盈。此外,粉刷天花板是一件神奇的事情,既不会太明显,也能影响空间的感觉。

questions.stem: What do people want upon returning home according to the passage?

options.text: To find pure white walls shining.
To enter a house well looked after.
To get a hug from family members.
To see cheerful colours all around.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：When people return home, they want to see colours that cheer them up and give them a hug.信号：want 直陈诉求 。录音用 they want to see colours that cheer them up 直接点出回家想要什么，want to 后面就是答题落点；紧接着 Pure white walls …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：To find pure white walls shining. 盗用了原文里 Pure white walls 这个原词，但原文紧接着说 Pure white walls simply don't do that.，白墙恰恰是被否定的、不能给人拥抱的东西，听到 white walls 就选正好掉坑。 借用原文：They don't look after you.
optionAnalysis.B: 偷换概念：To enter a house well looked after. 借用了原文 They don't look after you. 里的 look after，但原文说的是色彩照顾人（you），不是人想进入一座被照看好的房子，主语和对象都被偷换了。 借用原文：give them a hug
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：To get a hug from family members. 用了原文的 hug，但原文是 give them a hug——给拥抱的是色彩，根本没提 family members，把拥抱的来源安给了原文没说的家人。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（colours that cheer them up ↔ cheerful colours 动词转形容词）

questions.evidenceText: When people return home, they want to see colours that cheer them up and give them a hug.

questions.stem: What does the passage say people should avoid doing in home decoration?

options.text: Choosing a colour because it is fashionable.
Painting the interior of their cupboards.
Doing the painting job all by themselves.
Designing all window frames the same way.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P5）：Don't go for a colour because it's in fashion, or you've seen it in a magazine.信号：Don't 否定建议 。录音用祈使否定句 Don't go for a colour because it's in fashion 直接给出劝阻——别因为时髦而选色，Don't 就是该避免做法的信号词，这句即答案句。

optionAnalysis.B: 与原文相反：Painting the interior of their cupboards. 盗用了原文 the inside of a cupboard，但原文把刷柜子内部当作试色的好办法来推荐，而非要避免的事，态度正好相反。 借用原文：a bright window frame
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：Doing the painting job all by themselves. 里 all by themselves（亲力亲为）原文从未提及，录音只谈选什么色、刷哪里，没说该不该自己动手。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：Designing all window frames the same way. 借了原文出现过的 window frame（a bright window frame），但原文说的是把窗框作为试色的小空间，没说所有窗框要设计成同一款式，更没说要避免。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（because it's in fashion ↔ because it is fashionable 名词短语转形容词）

questions.evidenceText: Don't go for a colour because it's in fashion, or you've seen it in a magazine.

questions.stem: What can one do to make a room look bigger?

options.text: Fit most of the cupboards into walls.
Match the room's ceiling with all the furniture in colour.
Paint the wooden frameworks and walls the same colour.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P7）：One can also paint the wooden frameworks the same colour as the walls, helping the rooms look bigger.信号：helping…look bigger 因果 。录音里 paint the wooden frameworks the same colour as the walls 后面紧跟 helping the rooms …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：Fit most of the cupboards into walls. 借了原文反复出现的 cupboards，但原文谈柜子是说把柜子和墙刷同色（painting the overhead cupboards and the walls in the same colour），没说把柜子嵌进墙里，做法被改造成原文没说的内容。 借用原文：a painted ceiling is a magical thing without being too obvious
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：Hang landscape paintings all around. 里挂风景画原文完全没说，录音只谈刷颜色，没有任何挂画的内容。
optionAnalysis.C: 张冠李戴：Match the room's ceiling with all the furniture in colour. 借用了原文出现过的 ceiling（a painted ceiling）和同色概念，但原文让显大的同色是框架与墙，天花板只是另说能影响空间感，没说要与家具同色，把同色的双方张冠李戴。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（paint the wooden frameworks the same colour as the walls ↔ Paint the wooden frameworks and walls the same colour 近乎原句改写）

questions.evidenceText: One can also paint the wooden frameworks the same colour as the walls, helping the rooms look bigger.

transcript.text: Parents often hear that reading to their children is critical for supporting development, and the message is getting through to them. In fact, in the United States, a little over half of children between the ages of three and five were read to every day in 2007, and 83% of children in that age group in the same country were read to three or more times per week in 2012.
transcript.zh: 家长们经常听说给孩子读书对支持其发展至关重要，而且这一信息正在被他们接受。事实上，在美国，2007年有略高于一半的三至五岁儿童每天被朗读，而2012年同一国家该年龄段83%的儿童每周被朗读三次或更多次。

transcript.text: This is good news, because reading to young children helps their language and brain development. In fact, recent research has found that both the quality and quantity of shared book reading in infancy predicted later childhood vocabulary and reading skills. In other words, the more time parents spend reading, the greater the developmental benefits in their four-year-old children.
transcript.zh: 这是个好消息,因为给幼儿读书有助于他们的语言和大脑发育。事实上,最近的研究发现,婴儿期共享读书的质量和数量都能预测儿童后期的词汇量和阅读技能。换句话说,父母花在阅读上的时间越多,他们四岁孩子的发育益处就越大。

transcript.text: This is an important finding. But does it matter what books parents read? A new study has investigated this question. It followed infants across the second six months of life and found that when parents showed babies books that had faces or objects with specific labels, they learned more. This is in contrast to books that did not name images, or books that had the same label under each image. Books that named different characters also promoted greater learning. So what does this mean for parents? Not all books are created equal, so parents need to choose the books they share with their children with great care.
transcript.zh: 这是一个重要的发现。但父母读什么书重要吗?一项新研究调查了这个问题。该研究跟踪了婴儿生命中第二个六个月的情况,发现当父母给婴儿展示有面孔或带有特定标签的物体的书籍时,他们学到的更多。这与那些不标注图像名称的书籍或每张图像下都有相同标签的书籍形成对比。标注不同角色名称的书籍也促进了更多的学习。那么这对父母意味着什么呢?并非所有书籍都是一样的,因此父母需要非常谨慎地选择与孩子分享的书籍。

questions.stem: What does the passage say parents increasingly understand?

options.text: Children must read at least 3 times a week.
Reading is a habit every child can develop.
Reading to their children is important.
Children should start reading at age 3.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Parents often hear that reading to their children is critical for supporting development, and the message is getting through to them.信号：开篇点题句 + getting through 表领悟 。答案信号是开篇直接点题：reading to their children is critical for supporting development，紧跟…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 Children must read at least 3 times a week. 把原文 three or more times per week 的频次盗来，但原文说的是『父母给孩子读』的统计数据，不是『孩子自己必须每周读3次』的要求，答非所问。 借用原文：between the ages of three and five
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：选项 Reading is a habit every child can develop. 听起来很正确很顺耳，但全文只谈父母给孩子读书的好处与选书，从未说『阅读是每个孩子都能养成的习惯』，属凭常识脑补、原文无据。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 Children should start reading at age 3. 借用原文 between the ages of three and five 里的 three，但那是统计样本的年龄段，不是『孩子应3岁开始读书』的建议，数字真听到了、意思全拧了。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（reading to their children is critical for supporting development ↔ Reading to their children is important. critical=important 同义替换）

questions.evidenceText: Parents often hear that reading to their children is critical for supporting development, and the message is getting through to them.

questions.stem: What can predict children's reading skills according to recent research?

options.text: The number of books they have read by age four.
The speed of their brain development in infancy.
The number and quality of books parents read to them in infancy.
The quality and quantity of time parents spend playing with them.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：In fact, recent research has found that both the quality and quantity of shared book reading in infancy predicted later childhood vocabulary and reading skills.信号：研究发现信号 recent research has found + predicted 。答案信号是表研究结论的 recent research has found 和动词 predicted，predicted …

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 The number of books they have read by age four. 借用原文 four-year-old children 的 four，但原文 four 是说『四岁孩子身上的发展益处』，从没说『到四岁读了多少本书』能预测能力，数字听到了、意思编造了。 借用原文：reading to young children helps their language and brain development
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项 The speed of their brain development in infancy. 借了原文 brain development，但原文是说『读书有助于语言和大脑发育』，大脑发育是『结果/益处』，不是『预测阅读能力的原因』，把因果位置弄反了。 借用原文：the quality and quantity of shared book reading in infancy
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：选项 The quality and quantity of time parents spend playing with them. 几乎照抄原文的 quality and quantity 结构，却把核心动作从『读书』换成 playing（玩），原文谈的始终是 reading，不是陪玩，偷换了概念。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the quality and quantity of shared book reading in infancy ↔ The number and quality of books parents read to them in infancy. quantity=number、shared book reading=books parents read）

questions.evidenceText: In fact, recent research has found that both the quality and quantity of shared book reading in infancy predicted later childhood vocabulary and reading skills.

questions.stem: What kind of books are said to help babies learn more?

options.text: Books with pictures of dolls and toys.
Books describing the lives of animals.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：It followed infants across the second six months of life and found that when parents showed babies books that had faces or objects with specific labels, they learned more.信号：因果/条件句 when…they learned more 。答案信号是条件结果句 when parents showed babies books that had faces or objects with sp…

optionAnalysis.B: 过度推断：选项 Books with pictures of dolls and toys. 把原文 objects（物体）具体化为『玩偶和玩具』，原文从未指明是玩偶玩具，是凭常识把抽象的 objects 想象成具体玩具，属脑补。 借用原文：books that had faces or objects with specific labels
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：选项 Books describing the lives of animals. 看似贴近『讲动物』，但原文 P3 全程没提 animals，更没说『描写动物生活的书』有用，纯属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：选项 Books telling very interesting stories. 把『有用的书』偷换成『很有趣的故事书』，原文判定标准是『有没有具体标签』，不是『故事有不有趣』，换了一套评价维度。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（books that had faces or objects with specific labels ↔ Books with specifically labeled images. faces or objects=images、specific labels=specifically labeled）

questions.evidenceText: It followed infants across the second six months of life and found that when parents showed babies books that had faces or objects with specific labels, they learned more.

questions.stem: What are parents advised to do at the end of the passage?

options.text: Read as many books as possible to their children.
Choose carefully what to read to their children.
Create picture books for their children.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Not all books are created equal, so parents need to choose the books they share with their children with great care.信号：结尾因果建议句 so parents need to… 。答案信号是篇章结尾的因果建议句 so parents need to choose the books they share with their child…

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：选项 Read as many books as possible to their children. 主张『尽量多读』，但结尾恰恰强调 Not all books are created equal『书有好坏之分』、要『用心选』，方向与原文相反——原文要的是质而非量。 借用原文：the books they share with their children
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 Share experience with other parents. 借了一个似曾相识的 share，但原文的 share 是 the books they share with their children（与孩子共读书），从没说『与其他父母分享经验』，对象被换且原文无此建议。 借用原文：parents need to choose the books they share with their children
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：选项 Create picture books for their children. 借了原文反复出现的 books 和图像概念，但原文建议父母『挑选』书，从没说『为孩子创作绘本』，create 是无中生有的动作。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（choose the books they share with their children with great care ↔ Choose carefully what to read to their children. with great care=carefully、share=read to）

questions.evidenceText: Not all books are created equal, so parents need to choose the books they share with their children with great care.

Parenting brings fathers more joy than it does mothers, according to a new study. The research examined three studies 26______ more than 18,000 participants. Across all three, parenthood was 27______ with more positive wellbeing outcomes for dads than for mums.

So why are fathers happier than mothers? "Fathers may fare better than mothers in part due to how they spend time with their children," said lead author Katherine Nelson-Coffey. In one study, the authors 28______ that dads were more likely to take "playing" as an 29______ activity both when caring for their kids and spending time with their kids. "Playing with their children likely offers parents opportunities to experience positive feelings and 30______ closeness with their children," they say.

Fathers also did better than men without kids, reporting greater happiness, life satisfaction, and fewer 31______ symptoms. They also reported greater connectedness and autonomy(自主). For mums, 32______ , compared to women without children, the results weren't quite as positive. Mums reported greater autonomy, but also "greater trouble" and fewer positive 33______ .

Mums reported happier moods while interacting with their kids, compared to other experiences, but not while engaging 34______ in childcare. "This difference suggests that how mothers and fathers spend time with their children might have important 35______ for their wellbeing," the authors write. They suspect that mums may be less happy than dads because they're more likely to have higher expectations about parenthood. As such, they're more likely to be "let down" by the experience.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Not doing something will always be faster than doing it. This philosophy applies in many areas of life. For example, there is no meeting that goes faster than not having a meeting at all. This is not to say you should never attend another meeting, but the truth is that we say "yes" to too many things we don't actually want to do.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: How often do people ask you to do something and you just reply, "Sure." Three days later, you're overwhelmed by how much is on your to-do list. We become frustrated by our obligations even though we were the ones who said "yes" to them in the first place. Even worse, people will occasionally fight to do things that waste time. You don't have to do something just because it exists. It's worth asking if things are necessary. Many of them are not, and a simple "no" will be more productive than whatever work the most efficient person can cope with. But if the benefits of saying "no" are so obvious, then why do we say "yes" so often?

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: We say "yes" to many requests not because we want to do them, but because we don't want to be seen as rude or unhelpful. Often, we have to consider saying "no" to someone we will interact with again in the future—our co-worker, our spouse, our family and friends. Saying "no" to our superiors at work can be particularly difficult. In these situations, I like the approach recommended in Essentialism by Greg McKeown. He writes, "Remind your superiors what you would be neglecting if you said 'yes' and force them to deal with the trade-off. For example, if your manager comes to you and asks you to do X, you can respond with 'Yes, I'm happy to make this the priority. Which of these other projects should I deprioritize to pay attention to this new project?'"

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Collaborating with others is an important element of life. The thought of straining the relationship outweighs the commitment of our time and energy. For this reason, it can be helpful to be gracious in your response. Do whatever favors you can, and be warm-hearted and direct when you have to say no. But even after we have accounted for these social considerations, many of us still seem to do a poor job of managing the trade-off between yes and no. We find ourselves over-committed to things that don't meaningfully improve or support those around us, and certainly don't improve our own lives.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: Perhaps one issue is how we think about the meaning of yes and no. The words "yes" and "no" get so often used in comparison with each other that it feels like they carry equal weight in conversation. In reality, they're not just opposite in meaning, but of entirely different magnitudes in commitment. When you say "no", you're only saying "no" to one option. When you say "yes", you're saying "no" to every other option. I like how economist Tim Harford put it, "Every time we say 'yes' to a request, we're also saying 'no' to anything else we might accomplish with the time?" Once you're committed to something, you've already decided how that future block of time will be spent. In other words, saying "no" saves you time in the future. Saying "yes" costs you time in the future. "No" is a form of time credit. You retain the ability to spend your future time however you want. "Yes" is a form of time debt. You have to pay back your commitment at some point.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: "No" is a decision. "Yes" is a responsibility. Saying "no" is sometimes seen as a luxury that only those in power can afford. And it's true: turning down opportunities is easier when you can fall back on the safety net provided by power, money, and authority. But it's also true that saying "no" is not merely a privilege reserved for the successful. It's also a strategy that can help you become successful. Saying "no" is an important skill to develop at any stage of your career because it retains the most important asset in life: your time. As investor Pedro Sorrentino put it, "If you don't guard your time, people will steal it from you." You need to say "no" to whatever isn't leading you toward your goals.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: Nobody embodied this idea better than Steve Jobs, who said, "People think focus means saying 'yes' to the thing you've got to focus on. But that's not what it means at all. It means saying 'no' to the hundred other good ideas that there are. You have to pick carefully." Jobs had another great quote about saying "no": "I'm actually as proud of the things we haven't done as the things I have done. Innovation is saying 'no' to 1,000 things."

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Over time, as you continue to improve and succeed, your strategy needs to change. The opportunity cost of your time increases as you become more successful. At first, you just eliminate the obvious distractions and explore the rest. As your skills improve and you learn to separate what works from what doesn't, you have to continually increase your threshold for saying "yes". You still need to say "no" to distractions, but you also need to learn to say "no" to opportunities that were previously good uses of time, so you can make space for better uses of time. It's a good problem to have, but it can be a tough skill to master.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: What is true about health is also true about productivity: an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. More effort is wasted doing things that don't matter than is wasted doing things inefficiently. And if that is the case, elimination is a more useful skill than optimization. I'm reminded of the famous Peter Drucker quote, "There is nothing so useless as doing efficiently that which should not be done at all."

立春 (Start of Spring )在中国农历中表示春天的开始。立春之后， 白天变得更长，天气也愈发温暖，万物开始复苏，大地充满生机。人们常说"一年之计在于春"，农民在这个时节开始播种，为全年的丰收打下基础。中国人早在三千年前就己开始在立春这一天举行庆祝活动。数百年来，迎春一直是民间的重要习俗。在春暖花开的日子里，人们常常外出游玩，欣赏春天的美景。

Lichun (Start of Spring) marks the beginning of spring in the Chinese lunar calendar. After Lichun, the days grow longer and the weather becomes warmer; everything comes back to life, and the earth is full of vitality. As people often say, "The whole year's work depends on a good start in spring." At this time of year, farmers start sowing to lay the foundation for a good harvest throughout the whole year. In fact, the Chinese have started to hold celebrations on this day as early as 3,000 years ago. For centuries, welcoming spring has been an important folk custom. Today, on warm spring days when flowers are in full bloom, people often go out for outings to enjoy the beautiful scenery of spring.
